'''''Hypericum prolificum''''', known as '''shrubby St. John's wort''',<ref name=fna>{{eFloras|1|242416684|volume=6|Hypericum prolificum|first=Norman K. B. |last=Robson|access-date=2018-09-23}}</ref> is a [[deciduous]] shrub in the genus ''[[Hypericum]]''. It was named for its "prolific" number of [[stamen]]s.<ref name=gobotany>{{Go Botany|genus=Hypericum|species=prolificum|access-date=2018-09-23}}</ref>

==Description==
''Hypericum prolificum'' is a shrub growing up to {{convert|2|m|abbr=on}} tall with elliptic to oblanceolate leaves up to {{convert|70|mm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|15|mm|abbr=on}} broad.<ref name=hyp>{{Cite web|url=http://hypericum.myspecies.info/taxonomy/term/921|title=Hypericum prolificum|website=hypericum.myspecies.info|access-date=2018-10-21}}</ref> The flowerheads have between 1 and 9 flowers, each {{convert|15–30|mm|abbr=on}} across with 5 golden yellow petals and numerous stamens.<ref name=hyp/> The ovary is usually three-parted, though may have up to five parts in some individuals.<ref name=hyp/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Hypericum prolificum'' is [[native plant|native]] to the central and eastern [[United States]] and [[Ontario]].<ref name=fna/><ref name=usda>{{PLANTS|id=HYPY|taxon=Hypericum prolificum|access-date=2018-09-23}}</ref>  Habitats include [[riparian]] areas, slopes, thickets, swamp edges, and [[oak woodland]]s.<ref name=fna/><ref name=miflora>{{Michigan Flora|genus=Hypericum|species=prolificum|id=1466}}</ref>
